items.title: Greg Thomas interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 2014
items.q: the genetic works that Henry Louis Gates is doing through some companies, and these shows that he has on PBS where he looks at the genetic history of usually famous people shows that these mixtures are just reality.

ctx.x: I don’t know if I have a question here. But I wonder if —

If race, so-called, is a consideration either retrospectively or prospectively? Not race per se, because I’ve hired men, women, black, white, you know Latino, Asian — and they’ve been mixtures in the band, which is always great. But you do have to take a look at fit. When I say fit, fit could be stylistic fit, fit could be generational, because who’s your audience? As a writer it’s like you’ve got to be aware of who your audience is so when you’re booking/producing, who’s your audience? Now your audience in your…
considerations certainly because — certainly not race. But you do want to have the right fit for what you’re trying to present.
